questions.question: What affects stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on how fast you are driving. The faster you go, the longer it takes to stop.

questions.question: If you are unsure whether your vehicle fits under a bridge, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle fits under an overhead object, slow down and find another route if possible.

questions.question: For normal stopping power on vehicles with a front brake limiting valve, you should:

options.text: Set the control to the off position
Keep the control at the halfway mark

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Keep this valve in the "normal" position at all times for proper braking.

questions.question: What does a "Maximum Safe Speed" sign mean?

options.text: It is a suggestion only; you may drive faster
It applies only to vehicles weighing more than 26,000 pounds
You must not drive faster than the posted speed

questions.correctAnswerText: You must not drive faster than the posted speed
questions.explanation: Never exceed the speed shown on a "Maximum Safe Speed" sign.

questions.question: Emergency brakes are required on:

options.text: They are not required on trucks

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must work by mechanical force.

questions.question: When backing a vehicle, you should:

options.text: Move quickly to get out of the way
Try not to use your mirrors

questions.explanation: Backing a large vehicle is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Always use a helper if you can.

questions.question: If a traffic light has been green for a long time, what will likely happen?

options.text: It will change directly from green to red

questions.explanation: When a traffic light has been green for a long time, it will likely turn yellow soon. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light is red. It may also have a buzzer sound.

questions.question: When does a large combination vehicle take the longest to stop?
questions.explanation: Large combination vehicles take longer to stop when they are empty. The lighter weight causes the wheels to have less grip on the road.

questions.question: After completing a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Leave the emergency line valve open
Leave the rear shut-off valves open

questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency and service line valves to check for air. Then close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, what should you do?

options.text: The parking brake should not be engaged.
The gearshift should be in first gear.

questions.explanation: Before checking the engine compartment, turn on the parking brake and block the wheels. Check the engine before getting in the cab and starting the engine.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: It keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
questions.explanation: On combination vehicles with air brakes, the tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system. This happens if the trailer develops a bad leak or breaks away from the tractor.

questions.question: What happens because of the crack-the-whip effect?

options.text: Doubles and triples are more likely to roll over than other combination vehicles.
A combination vehicle makes a loud noise when driven fast.
The tires on a middle trailer lock up at every stop.
Vehicles following a truck can travel faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubles and triples are more likely to roll over than other combination vehicles.
questions.explanation: Double and triple trailers are more likely to roll over because of the crack-the-whip effect. Drivers should know about rearward amplification for their vehicles and steer carefully.

questions.question: When driving a double, where should the lightest trailer go?
questions.explanation: For safer handling of doubles or triples, put the heavier trailer right behind the tractor. Put the lighter trailer in the rear position.

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, brake drums should not have cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums during your walk-around inspection before starting a trip. It is unsafe to drive if a brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Any glad hand can connect to any other glad hand.
Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.explanation: When coupling, connect matching glad hands. They are often color-coded to help drivers avoid mistakes. Blue is typically used for service lines and red for emergency lines.

questions.question: What should you do if the air pressure warning light comes on while driving?

options.text: Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.
Safely leave the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely leave the road and stop.
questions.explanation: If the air pressure warning light or buzzer comes on while driving, stop immediately and park safely. This warning means there is a problem in the air brake system that needs to be fixed.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. It is so clear that you can see the road through it, which makes the road look wet.

questions.question: When driving a double or triple, what is important to remember?

options.text: The vehicle needs more space than most other vehicles.
Other drivers will get out of your way when needed.
The vehicle weighs the same as other vehicles.
The vehicle can fit easily into small spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle needs more space than most other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Doubles and triples need more space than other vehicles. They are longer and their size and weight make it hard to turn or stop quickly. Always make sure you have enough space before entering traffic, crossing, or changing lanes.

questions.question: How do you release dolly brakes?
questions.explanation: Release dolly brakes by opening the air tank petcock. If the dolly has spring brakes, use the dolly parking brake control.
